scope: Post-election guide with a dated national discovery summary and selected local cases. The September 21 snapshot is retained as history. Selected November results are paired with official ballot, legal-effect or results records and explicitly labeled where certification has not been verified. Not an exhaustive ballot database, a national opinion poll or a personalized sample ballot. No automatic election-results feed is connected.

snapshot.limit: Source publication date, not a live count. Local measures do not apply to every voter in the listed state. An unlisted state is not a verified zero. The national totals are separate from the four detailed examples.

measures.title: Question 1 · A new land use
measures.effect: Changes which uses voters authorize in this area
measures.summary: Voters rejected adding data centers to the authorized uses in the Eldorado Valley Transfer Area outside its habitat-conservation easement.
measures.yes: Allow data centers as a permitted use in the specified area. The council could consider future leases.
measures.no: Keep data centers outside the authorized uses in that area.
measures.limit: This question covers the specified Eldorado Valley Transfer Area outside the conservation easement, not all land in Boulder City or nearby federal land. A YES result would only have authorized a use, not approved a facility or required a lease. Campaign arguments are advocacy, not environmental measurements.
measures.question: What would each future lease require for water, electricity, noise, emissions and public infrastructure costs?

measures.title: Measure NDC · A citywide prohibition
measures.summary: A General Plan amendment to prohibit data centers throughout Monterey Park, with the prohibition continuing until voters end it.
measures.yes: Adopt the proposed citywide prohibition through the General Plan amendment.
measures.no: Do not adopt this proposed General Plan amendment.
measures.outcome: City update identifies Measure NDC as adopted. No certified vote tally is reproduced here.
measures.limit: A no vote would not itself approve a project or remove other applicable restrictions. The ballot’s stated health and utility-rate purposes are not measured health outcomes.
measures.question: How is the city implementing the prohibition, and how does it define the facilities covered?

measures.title: Tax-increment districts · Who gets the next vote?
measures.effect: Adds a referendum requirement for qualifying districts
measures.summary: An ordinance requiring voter approval before the city creates or approves specified tax-increment districts involving large capital expenditures or the stated $10 million thresholds.
measures.yes: Require a referendum before approving a district covered by the ordinance.
measures.no: Do not add this referendum requirement through the proposed ordinance.
measures.outcome: Election-night county report: 2,710 yes and 1,371 no. This is the April 7 report, not a certified canvass verified by this dashboard.
measures.limit: This is a financing and approval-process measure, not a general data-center ban. Consult the full text for the distinct base-value and project-cost thresholds; it does not establish a campus’s tax payment.
measures.question: Which future financing districts are covered, and who bears repayment and infrastructure risks?

measures.title: High-impact facilities · A ten-year prohibition
measures.effect: Prohibits covered facilities within the city for ten years, subject to voter amendment or repeal.
measures.summary: A voter-approved prohibition on high-impact data centers and specified battery energy storage systems.
measures.yes: Adopt the ten-year prohibition on covered data centers and battery storage systems.
measures.no: Do not adopt this proposed prohibition through the ballot question.
measures.outcome: The City reported approval on November 4, with approximately 70% support. No exact certified tally is reproduced here.
measures.resultStatus: Approval and implementation reported by the City; certified vote tally not independently verified.
measures.legalEffect: Binding city prohibition. The City states it takes effect immediately and lasts ten years unless voters amend or repeal it.
measures.nextStep: Ask the City how the definitions and enforcement apply to a particular proposal, including storage projects; monitor implementation rather than treating the previous temporary moratorium as the only protection.
measures.limit: City scope, not all of Butler County or Kansas. High-impact data centers exceed 10 MW peak electrical load OR 100,000 gallons daily water draw. The measure also prohibits Tier 2 and Tier 3 battery storage, described by the City as aggregate capacity greater than 80 kWh. These thresholds define covered facilities; they are not measurements of an actual project's use or health effects.
measures.question: Which proposals meet the exact definitions, and how will the City document compliance and enforcement?

measures.title: Measure DB · Who can change the ban?
measures.effect: Affirms an existing citywide ban as a voter-approved ordinance.
measures.summary: The measure would affirm the Council's existing data-center prohibition in every city zone and reserve amendment or repeal to voters.
measures.yes: Adopt the voter-approved ordinance affirming the citywide data-center prohibition.
measures.no: Do not adopt this voter-approved ordinance; the Council-adopted ban would remain unless the Council later changed it.
measures.outcome: The official county count as of November 17 at 15:58:36 reports 19,157 YES (83.92%) and 3,671 NO (16.08%). Certification was not verified here.
measures.resultStatus: Official county count; certification and final municipal attestation not independently verified.
measures.legalEffect: Binding ordinance if adopted and certified; the City Attorney says future amendment or repeal would require voters. The Council's existing prohibition already applies.
measures.nextStep: Check the certified result and municipal attestation, then confirm how the City applies the data-center definition and its incidental-use exception.
measures.limit: Alhambra city limits only. The definition excludes data facilities incidental to another primary use and strictly supporting its on-site operations. The official city analysis explains that a NO vote would not remove the existing Council-adopted ban. A vote tally does not measure emissions avoided.
measures.question: Has the result been certified and attested, and how is the incidental-use exception interpreted?

measures.title: Amendment 4 · A charter-level prohibition
measures.effect: Prohibits new data centers within the city and requires voters to amend or repeal the charter prohibition.
measures.summary: A city charter amendment concerning approval, construction, expansion and operation of new data centers.
measures.yes: Adopt the charter prohibition and require voter approval to amend or repeal it.
measures.no: Do not add this charter prohibition through Amendment 4.
measures.outcome: The county results portal records 7,884 YES (77.20%) and 2,328 NO (22.80%) for Amendment 4. The county election office labels its linked November 3 results official.
measures.resultStatus: Official county results; exact certification date not recorded here.
measures.legalEffect: Binding charter restriction. Ordinance 2026-O-18 makes approved amendments effective upon certification; the exact certification date was not verified here.
measures.nextStep: Ask the City Clerk for the certified result and updated charter, and how the new charter restriction operates alongside the separately adopted data-center moratorium.
measures.limit: Corporate limits of Edgewater, Florida only. The ballot ordinance defines covered facilities and makes the prohibition self-executing; it is not a Florida-wide ban. Ordinance adoption placing a question on the ballot is distinct from voter approval and certification. The separate September 14 moratorium should not be mistaken for this charter amendment.
measures.question: Where is the certified charter update, and which facilities and applications fall within its definition?

measures.title: Moratorium question · Advice requires a next step
measures.effect: Asks whether the City should implement a moratorium; does not itself enact one.
measures.summary: An advisory question on whether Bloomington should pause creation of large-scale data centers.
measures.yes: Advise the City to implement a moratorium on creation of large-scale data centers.
measures.outcome: Ballotpedia reports approval. The official ballot confirms advisory wording; the official canvass was not independently verified here.
measures.legalEffect: Nonbinding advisory vote; separate municipal action is required to establish a moratorium. Illinois Election Code 5/28-6(c) gives these advisory questions no legal effect.
measures.nextStep: Look for a separate City Council proposal, public hearing or adopted ordinance, and ask how officials plan to respond to the advisory result.
measures.limit: The question concerns the City of Bloomington, Illinois. It expresses an opinion on a large-scale-data-center moratorium; it sets no duration or detailed standards and does not prove that a moratorium is currently in force. The Illinois advisory rule should not be generalized to binding measures in other states.
measures.question: What separate City action, if any, has implemented the recommendation?

postElection.byStateScope: All 57 measures tracked for 2026, including earlier elections and four pending measures; not the 47 November 3 measures alone.
postElection.limit: Secondary-source discovery aggregate, not an independent canvass of all results. The 47 November 3 measures include 10 nonbinding advisory questions. Favoring limits describes the direction of a local outcome, not a count of binding bans or a national opinion poll. Different questions have different legal effects; certification and implementation must be checked locally. State totals cover the full 2026 tracker. An unlisted state is not a verified zero.
